text:
**Yes, some can, but many can't.** A power station only works as a UPS if it has a documented UPS/EPS mode with automatic switchover, and the switchover has to be fast enough for your computer.

**What to check**
- **Transfer time:** EcoFlow says many products advertise UPS but take 20-30 ms to switch, and it argues that's risky for desktops and drives ([EcoFlow](https://www.ecoflow.com/us/blog/use-portable-power-station-as-ups-power-supply)). Anker is less alarmist. It says 10-20 ms works for some devices, but it isn't the 0 ms of an online UPS, so check your device's manual ([Anker](https://www.ankersolix.com/blogs/home-power-backup/portable-power-station-ups-home-server-nas)). None of the sources say what your specific PC tolerates, so check your power supply's specs.
- **Pure sine wave output** is preferred for computers ([Anker](https://www.ankersolix.com/blogs/portable-power-station/can-a-portable-power-station-be-used-as-a-ups)).
- **Pass-through:** confirm the manufacturer supports charging and powering devices at the same time. Pass-through alone isn't UPS protection.
- **Wattage:** add up your computer's measured draw and compare it with the continuous output rating. A plug-in watt meter helps.
- **Runtime estimate:** watt-hours × ~0.85 ÷ load in watts. A 1,000 Wh unit running a 100 W load gives roughly 8.5 hours at best.

**Options with a listed switchover time**
- **BLUETTI Elite 30 V2**: ≤10 ms, 288 Wh, 600 W. It's the cheapest option and suits a laptop or small setup. $289.99, or $275.50 with code AFF5OFF. [Buy](https://dealectric.com/go/bluetti-elite-30-v2)
- **ALLPOWERS P1800**: ≤10 ms, 1,024 Wh, 1,800 W. $439, or $395.10 with code ALLPOWERS26. The store page contradicts itself (product images say 15 ms), so verify before buying. [Buy](https://dealectric.com/go/allpowers-p1800-1024wh)
- **BLUETTI Elite 200 V2**: ≤15 ms, 2,073.6 Wh, 2,600 W. It's suited to a computer plus a router and more. $899, or $854.05 with AFF5OFF. [Buy](https://dealectric.com/go/bluetti-elite-200-v2)
- **Anker SOLIX S2000**: 10 ms, 2,010 Wh, 1,500 W pure sine wave, $699.99 after coupon. [Product info](https://www.ankersolix.com/blogs/portable-power-station/can-a-portable-power-station-be-used-as-a-ups)
- **EcoFlow RIVER 3 Plus**: <10 ms, 600 W, described as NAS-compliant. I didn't get a price or purchase page for it. [Details](https://www.ecoflow.com/us/blog/use-portable-power-station-as-ups-power-supply)
- **BLUETTI AC180 and AC200L** list 20 ms, so I'd skip them for a computer. [AC180](https://dealectric.com/go/bluetti-ac180), [AC200L](https://dealectric.com/go/bluetti-ac200l)

The BLUETTI and ALLPOWERS links are affiliate links, and Dealectric is paid if you buy. The sources I have don't cover the pricing of EcoFlow or Anker models beyond what's above.

**Bottom line:** For a typical home PC, a 10 ms unit is a reasonable choice if you confirm the UPS/pass-through mode and size it to your load. If your device's manual requires 0 ms transfer, or the data is critical, buy a true online UPS instead. Either way, save your work and shut down gracefully if the outage runs long.

If you tell me your computer's wattage and how long you want it to run on battery, I can narrow this down.
